questions.stem:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a straight row facing North.
• D sits at the extreme left end.
• A is 3rd from the left.
• E sits immediately to the left of A.
• B sits immediately to the right of A.
• C sits at the extreme right end.
(F occupies the remaining seat.)

Who is 2nd from the right end?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Arrangement (left to right): D(1) E(2) A(3) B(4) F(5) C(6). 2nd from right = position 5 = F. Trap: B is at position 4 (3rd from right), so students who count from the right might pick B.

questions.stem:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a straight row facing North.
Arrangement: D  E  A  B  F  C  (left to right)

How many persons sit between D and B?
questions.explanation: B is correct. D is at position 1 and B is at position 4. Between them are E(2) and A(3) = 2 persons. Trap: students sometimes count D and B themselves, giving 4.

questions.stem:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a straight row facing North.
Arrangement: D  E  A  B  F  C  (left to right)

Who sits immediately to the left of C?
questions.explanation: D is correct. C is at position 6 (extreme right). The person at position 5 = F sits immediately to C's left. Trap: B is at position 4, two seats from C — students confuse 'immediate' with 'nearby'.

questions.stem:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a straight row facing North.
Original arrangement: D  E  A  B  F  C  (left to right)

E and B exchange seats; A and F also exchange seats. Who is now at position 4 from the left?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Original: D(1) E(2) A(3) B(4) F(5) C(6). After E↔B: D(1) B(2) A(3) E(4) F(5) C(6). After A↔F: D(1) B(2) F(3) E(4) A(5) C(6). Position 4 = E. Trap: applying only one swap gives B or A at position 4.

questions.stem:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a straight row facing North.
Original arrangement: D  E  A  B  F  C  (positions 1–6, left to right)

All persons shift one position to the right; the person at the extreme right (C) moves to the extreme left. Who is now at position 4?
questions.explanation: A is correct. After the circular right-shift: C moves to position 1, and everyone else shifts right by 1: C(1) D(2) E(3) A(4) B(5) F(6). Position 4 = A. Trap: B ends up at position 5 (not 4); students who shift only some persons may pick E or D.

questions.stem:
Five students P, Q, R, S, T are ranked by marks scored in a test.
• P scored more than Q but less than R.
• T scored the highest among all five.
• S scored less than Q.
• R did not score the highest.

Who is ranked 4th from the top?
questions.explanation: B is correct. From the clues: S < Q < P < R < T (T highest, S lowest). Ranking top-to-bottom: T(1st), R(2nd), P(3rd), Q(4th), S(5th). 4th from top = Q. Trap: S is 5th (not 4th), and P is 3rd (not 4th).

questions.stem:
Five students P, Q, R, S, T scored in a test. Their order from lowest to highest is: S < Q < P < R < T.

How many students scored fewer marks than P?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Order: S < Q < P < R < T. Students below P: Q and S — exactly 2. Trap: 3 students (adding R or T by mistake) is a common over-count.

questions.stem: Five students are ranked S < Q < P < R < T (lowest to highest). Each successive student from the bottom scored exactly 8 marks more than the one below. If S scored 45 marks, what did T score?
questions.explanation: C is correct. S=45, Q=53, P=61, R=69, T=77. Each step adds 8: 45+8=53+8=61+8=69+8=77. Trap: 73 adds only 7 per step; 75 computes T=S+4×8−3 erroneously.

questions.stem: Five students are ranked S < Q < P < R < T (lowest to highest). P is exactly between which two students in terms of rank?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Ranking top-to-bottom: T(1) R(2) P(3) Q(4) S(5). P is at rank 3, flanked by R(rank 2) above and Q(rank 4) below. Trap: 'T and Q' skips R; 'R and S' skips Q.

questions.stem:
Original ranking (lowest to highest): S < Q < P < R < T.
In a second test:
• R scores more than T.
• Q scores more than P.
• P scores more than T.
• S still has the lowest score.
Which of the following is a valid ranking (highest to lowest) for the second test?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Constraints: R>T, Q>P, P>T, S=lowest. Check A: R>Q>P>T>S. R>T ✓; Q>P ✓; P>T ✓; S lowest ✓. Check B: T>R violates R>T. Check C: T>R violates R>T. Check D: S is not lowest (S>T>P). Only A satisfies all conditions.
